\chapter{Glossary}
\markboth{Glossary}{Glossary}
% Generated by tools/assemble_glossary.py from appendices/glossary/*-terms.tex. Do not edit by hand;
% edit the per-chapter term files and re-run the script.
This glossary collects the terms that the book sets in bold when it defines them. Each entry
names the chapter that introduces the term; a term used in several chapters points to the first.

\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=1.5em,itemsep=2pt]
\item[Activation length $\ell_{\mathrm{act}}$] The link length, below the communication range $R_{\mathrm{comm}}$, at which the soft range term of the preferred velocity starts to pull a drone towards its nearest teammate. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Active constraint] An inequality constraint that holds with equality at the solution and has a positive Lagrange multiplier; it is the constraint that shapes the solution. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[ADE / FDE / minADE$_K$] Average displacement error, the mean Euclidean error over the prediction horizon, and final displacement error, the error at the last step, with per-horizon versions $\mathrm{ADE}_h$, $\mathrm{FDE}_h$; $\mathrm{minADE}_K$ and $\mathrm{minFDE}_K$ score the best of $K$ sampled trajectories and are not comparable with the ADE/FDE of a deterministic predictor. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Adjacency list] A representation of a graph that stores, for every vertex, the list of its neighbours together with the edge weights. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Admissible heuristic] A heuristic that never overestimates, $0\le\hcost(n)\le\hcost^*(n)$; it guarantees that \astar with re-opening returns an optimal path. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Admissible velocity] A velocity from which the robot can still stop before the nearest obstacle on its rollout: $v\le\sqrt{2\,\dist\,a_b}$, or $v\dt+v^2/(2a_b)\le\dist$ when the command is held for one interval before braking starts. The rotational condition $\abs{\omega}\le\sqrt{2\,\dist\,\dot\omega_b}$ of Fox et al.\ is a heuristic cap rather than a braking bound: the braking argument for the rotation uses the heading change $\Delta\theta=\abs{\omega}\dist/v$ still available, not the free distance itself. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[ADMM] The alternating direction method of multipliers, a first-order splitting method for convex problems; the OSQP iteration used by the book's QP solver. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Agent] One of the $k$ entities of a MAPF instance, with its own start vertex and goal vertex. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Agent-centred frame] The input normalisation in which the last observed position is the origin, the last heading is the $x$-axis and displacements are divided by a typical step length; it makes the predictor translation and rotation invariant. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Algebraic connectivity] The second-smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_2$ of the graph Laplacian $\mat{L}=\mat{D}-\mat{A}$; it is positive iff the graph is connected and sets the convergence rate of consensus, while $\lambda_n\le2d_{\max}$ bounds the safe step size. \ (\cref{ch:appB}, \cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Angle wrapping] Mapping an angle to $(-\pi, \pi]$ with $\operatorname{wrap}(\theta) = \theta - 2\pi\lceil(\theta - \pi)/(2\pi)\rceil$; applied to every difference of angles in an innovation, a residual or a likelihood, and to the heading after every update. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Anytime algorithm] An algorithm that returns a first solution quickly and improves it for as long as it is allowed to run. \ (\cref{ch:ch01}, \cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Anytime D*] The combination of \arastar with \dstarlite: an anytime planner whose $\gcost$/$\rhs$ bookkeeping also repairs the search when edge costs change, inflating the keys of overconsistent states only. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Apex (of a velocity obstacle)] The vertex of the wedge, at $\vel_B$ for a velocity obstacle, at the origin for a static obstacle and at $(\vel_A+\vel_B)/2$ for a reciprocal velocity obstacle. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Artificial potential field] A scalar function $U(\pos)$ over the free space, low at the goal and high near obstacles, whose negative gradient $-\nabla U$ is used as the velocity (or force) command of a robot. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Asymptotic optimality] The property that the cost of the best path in the tree converges to the optimal cost $c^*$ with probability one as the number of samples grows; \rrtstar has it, \rrt does not. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Attention] The operation $\operatorname{softmax}(\mat{Q}\mat{K}\T/\sqrt{d_k})\mat{V}$ that returns for every query a convex combination of the values weighted by the similarity of the query to the keys; over time steps it replaces recurrence, over agents it models interaction, at cost $\Theta(n^2 d)$. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Attractive potential] The goal term $U_{\mathrm{att}}=\tfrac12 k_{\mathrm{att}}\norm{\pos-\pos_{\mathrm{g}}}^2$ (quadratic) or $k_{\mathrm{att}}d^*\norm{\pos-\pos_{\mathrm{g}}}-\tfrac12 k_{\mathrm{att}}(d^*)^2$ beyond the switch distance $d^*$ (conic); the hybrid of the two keeps the force bounded far away and smooth at the goal. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Back set] The set of all nodes from which a node has been generated; it must contain every parent, not only the cheapest one, for backpropagation to be complete. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Backpropagation (of collision sets)] Passing a collision set from a node to every node in its back set, recursively, and re-opening every node whose set grew so that it is expanded again with more neighbours. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Backward Dijkstra] A run of Dijkstra's algorithm from the goal over the graph with every edge reversed, which yields the distance to the goal from every vertex. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[BCBS$(w_H,w_L)$] Bounded \cbs: focal search with factor $w_L$ at the low level and $w_H$ at the high level, the latter measured against the smallest cost in \Open instead of a lower bound; guarantee $w_Hw_L\,C^*$ only. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Bidirectional search] Two simultaneous waves, one forward from the source and one backward from the target, stopped when the sum of the two smallest queue keys reaches the cost of the best connecting path found. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Big-M constraint] The pair $\vect{a}\T\vect{z}\le\beta+Mb$, $b\in\set{0,1}$, with $M$ a large constant, which enforces a linear constraint when $b=0$ and switches it off when $b=1$; with a sum constraint on the binaries it expresses ``at least one of these constraints holds''. \ (\cref{ch:appB}, \cref{ch:ch22})
\item[BIT*] Batch informed trees: samples are drawn in batches inside the informed set and the implicit random geometric graph is searched with an edge queue ordered by $\hat f=\hat g+\hat h$ with lazy collision checks, reusing the search across batches. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Blocked layer $\mathcal{B}_t$] The set of grid cells that the predicted intruder may occupy at grid time $t$, the cells within the inflated radius plus half a cell of the predicted mean; the replanner treats them as blocked or expensive in time layer $t$ of the space-time graph. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Bootstrap filter] The particle filter that uses the motion model as its proposal distribution, so that each weight is multiplied by the likelihood $p(\meas_k \mid \state_k^{(i)})$ of the new measurement; also called sequential importance resampling (SIR). \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Bounded suboptimality] The guarantee that a solution costs at most $w$ times the optimal cost, for a factor $w\ge 1$ chosen by the user. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Bounded-suboptimal algorithm] An algorithm with a parameter $w\ge1$ that returns, on every solvable instance, a solution of cost at most $w\,C^*$ without computing the optimum $C^*$; $w$ is the suboptimality factor. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Braking candidate] The command that keeps the current direction and reduces the speed by $a_b\dt$; it always lies in the window and is admissible whenever the previous command was, so DWA never runs out of safe options with static obstacles. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Braking distance] The distance $v^2/(2a_b)$ covered while decelerating from speed $v$ at the constant rate $a_b$ to a standstill. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Branch-and-bound] The exact MILP search that solves LP relaxations, branches on a fractional integer variable and discards subproblems whose bound cannot beat the incumbent. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Branch-and-bound pruning] Deleting tree vertices with $\mathrm{Cost}(v)+\norm{x_{\mathrm{goal}}-v}\ge c_{\mathrm{best}}$, which can never lie on a better path; used in anytime \rrtstar. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Branch-and-cut] Branch-and-bound strengthened by cutting planes, valid inequalities that cut off fractional relaxation optima, plus presolve and primal heuristics, as in HiGHS. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Breadth-first search] The unit-cost special case of Dijkstra's algorithm in which a first-in-first-out queue replaces the heap. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Bypass] An ICBS improvement: when a child has the same cost as its parent and fewer conflicts, the parent adopts the child's paths instead of being split, so a non-cardinal conflict is removed without growing the tree. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Cactus plot] For each strategy, the number of runs finished with effort at most $x$ plotted against $x$; it shows the whole runtime distribution and the success rate at once. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Calibration] Agreement between a nominal probability $p$ and the fraction of true positions that fall inside the predicted $p$-ellipse; learned predictors are often over-confident and need a per-horizon inflation factor fitted on validation data. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Cardinal conflict] A conflict whose resolution raises the cost of the node in both children; semi-cardinal if only one child's cost rises, non-cardinal if neither does. Splitting cardinal conflicts first keeps the constraint tree small. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Chance constraint] A constraint required to hold with probability at least $1-\delta$; for a Gaussian predicted intruder it becomes the half-plane constraint with the radius inflated by $\kappa_\delta\sqrt{\vect{n}_k\T\mat{\Sigma}_k\vect{n}_k}$. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[ChooseParent] The \rrtstar step that connects the new vertex to the near vertex giving the smallest cost-to-come through a collision-free segment, with the nearest vertex as fallback. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Classical MAPF] The multi-agent path finding problem on an undirected graph with discrete time, synchronous unit-time move and wait actions, distinct starts and goals, stay-at-target, and vertex and swapping conflicts forbidden. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Clearance] The distance $\rho(\pos)$ from the robot position to the nearest point of an obstacle; $\nabla\rho$ is the unit vector pointing away from that point. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Clearance term] The free distance of the rollout divided by $d_{\max}$; it rewards open space ahead of the robot. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Collision checking by subdivision] Testing points spaced at most $\delta$ apart along a segment against the obstacles inflated by $r+\delta/2$; every accepted segment then has clearance at least the robot radius $r$. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Collision cone] $CC_{A|B}$, the set of relative velocities whose ray from the origin meets the disc of radius $r_A+r_B$ around $\pos_{\mathrm{rel}}$; a wedge of half-angle $\arcsin\bigl((r_A+r_B)/\norm{\pos_{\mathrm{rel}}}\bigr)$ bounded by the tangent rays. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Collision rate] The fraction of runs in which some pair of agents comes closer than the sum of their radii; a proportion, reported with a Wilson interval and, when it is zero, bounded by the rule of three. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Collision set] The set $C(v)$ of agents that are allowed to branch over all their moves at the node $v$; it starts empty, receives the agents involved in collisions found below $v$, and only grows. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Communication graph] The graph $G=(V,E)$ whose vertices are the drones and whose edges join pairs that can exchange messages; for a radio of range $R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ it is the radius graph with $\{i,j\}\in E$ iff $\norm{\pos_i-\pos_j}\le R_{\mathrm{comm}}$, and it changes as the drones move. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Completeness] The property of finding a solution whenever one exists; in the strong form the algorithm also reports failure when no solution exists, which needs a finite search space or a separate feasibility test. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Condensed QP] The form of the MPC problem in which the predicted states are eliminated with $\mat{X}=\mat{S}_x\state_0+\mat{S}_u\mat{U}$, leaving a dense quadratic program in the stacked inputs $\mat{U}$ alone. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Conditional Gaussian] For jointly Gaussian $(\state_a,\state_b)$, the distribution $\state_a\mid\state_b\sim\Normal(\vect{\mu}_a+\mat{\Sigma}_{ab}\mat{\Sigma}_{bb}\inv(\state_b-\vect{\mu}_b),\,\mat{\Sigma}_{aa}-\mat{\Sigma}_{ab}\mat{\Sigma}_{bb}\inv\mat{\Sigma}_{ba})$; the Kalman update is this formula applied to a state and a linear measurement of it. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Configuration space] The set of all positions (configurations) of a robot; it splits into the free part $\Cfree$ and the obstacle part $\Cobs$. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Conflict heuristic $h_c$] The number of vertex and swapping conflicts in the paths of a CT node, or of a partial low-level path with the other agents' current paths; the secondary heuristic of \ecbs at both levels. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Conflict re-check] The run of the conflict detector over the padded paths of all drones, from the current grid time on, after any change of a path in force (a replan, a repair or a delayed reconnection). \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Conflict splitting] Resolving a conflict $\langle a_i, a_j, v, t\rangle$ by generating two children, one with $\langle a_i, v, t\rangle$ and one with $\langle a_j, v, t\rangle$, and replanning only the constrained agent in each; every valid solution satisfies at least one of the two constraints. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Conflict-based search (CBS)] A two-level optimal MAPF algorithm: the high level searches a binary constraint tree best-first on the sum of costs, the low level plans one agent at a time with space-time \astar under that agent's constraints. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Conflict-graph heuristic (CG)] An admissible high-level heuristic for \cbs: the size of a minimum vertex cover of the graph whose vertices are agents and whose edges are cardinal conflicts, a lower bound on the cost increase needed to resolve them. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Connection radius] $r_n=\min\{\gamma_{\rrtstar}(\log n/n)^{1/d},\eta\}$ with $n$ the number of tree vertices; asymptotic optimality needs $\gamma_{\rrtstar}>2(1+1/d)^{1/d}(\mu(\Xfree)/\zeta_d)^{1/d}$, and the schedule keeps the expected \textsc{Near} set at $\bigO{\log n}$ vertices. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Connectivity maintenance] Keeping the communication graph connected while the drones move, by constraining the edges of a spanning subgraph to stay shorter than $R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ or by a potential that becomes infinite at the range boundary; monitored through $\lambda_2$. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Consensus protocol] $\dot{\vect{x}}_i=\sum_{j\in N_i}(\vect{x}_j-\vect{x}_i)$, i.e.\ $\dot{\vect{x}}=-\mat{L}\vect{x}$; on a connected undirected graph every state converges to the average of the initial states. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Consistent heuristic] A heuristic with $\hcost(\gamma)=0$ and $\hcost(n)\le c(n,n')+\hcost(n')$ on every edge (also called monotone); it is admissible, and with it \astar expands every node at most once and pops nodes in non-decreasing order of $\fcost$. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Constant-velocity baseline] Extrapolation of the last observed position with a velocity estimated from the last $k$ intervals; exact on straight flight, with a noise error that grows like $h/k$, and the baseline every learned predictor must beat. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Constant-velocity model] The kinematic model with state $(\pos,\vel)$, $\pos_k=\pos_{k-1}+\dt\,\vel_{k-1}$, $\vel_k=\vel_{k-1}$, whose unknown accelerations are treated as process noise. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Constraint tree (CT)] The binary tree searched by the high level of \cbs; each node holds a set of constraints, one shortest path per agent that respects them, and the sum of those path costs. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Convex function] A function whose graph lies below every chord, $f(\theta\vect{x}+(1-\theta)\vect{y})\le\theta f(\vect{x})+(1-\theta)f(\vect{y})$; every local minimum of a convex function on a convex set is global, and a twice differentiable function is convex iff its Hessian is positive semidefinite everywhere. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Cooperative A*] Silver's name for space-time \astar against a reservation table, with the goal-stay test and a horizon; the low-level search of prioritized planning. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Coordinated-turn model] The motion model with state $(x, y, v, \psi, \omega)$, constant speed $v$ and constant turn rate $\omega$, whose position update follows a circular arc of radius $v/\abs{\omega}$; nonlinear through $v\cos\psi$, $v\sin\psi$ and the division by $\omega$. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Corner cutting] A diagonal move on an 8-connected grid that passes the corner of an obstacle cell; the book forbids it because the swept disc of the robot would clip the obstacle. \ (\cref{ch:ch02}, \cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Corridor symmetry] Two agents traversing a narrow corridor in opposite directions; every possible waiting time becomes a separate branch unless a corridor constraint forces one agent to wait outside until the other has passed. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Cost-to-come] $\mathrm{Cost}(v)$, the length of the tree path from the start to vertex $v$; \rrtstar keeps $\mathrm{Cost}(v)=\mathrm{Cost}(\mathrm{parent}(v))+\norm{v-\mathrm{parent}(v)}$ as an invariant. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Covariance ellipse] The set of points at a fixed Mahalanobis distance from the mean of a Gaussian; its axes are the eigenvectors of the covariance and its semi-axes are the square roots of the eigenvalues. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[CT node] A triple $N = (N.\mathcal{C}, N.\pi, N.\cost)$; the root has no constraints, a goal node has a conflict-free solution, and a child adds exactly one constraint to its parent's set. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Curse of dimensionality] The growth of a uniform grid as $N^{d}$ with the resolution $N$ per axis and the dimension $d$, which makes grid search impossible in large 3D volumes and in state spaces that include velocities. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Cycle conflict] A rotation of $m\ge3$ agents that all move at the same time step, each into the distinct vertex that the next one is leaving, along a fully occupied cycle; allowed in this book. The degenerate case $m=2$ of the same pattern is the swapping conflict, which is why the cycle conflict is defined for $m\ge3$. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[D* Lite] \lpastar turned around to search backward from the goal, with a key modifier $k_m$ so that the robot may move while it replans; the replanning algorithm of the hybrid architecture. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Deadline] The time by which the replanning layer must deliver a path; an anytime planner meets it with the best path found so far, a fixed-budget optimal search may miss it altogether. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Degeneracy] The state of a particle filter in which a few particles carry almost all the weight after repeated weighting without resampling. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Deliberative method] A method that searches or optimises over possible futures, using a model of the world, before it acts. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Dense fallback] The remedy for an empty intersection of \orca half-planes: choose the velocity that minimises the largest violation over all agent half-planes while keeping the obstacle half-planes hard; van den Berg et al.\ call it the safest possible velocity, the one which penetrates the half-planes least. It is a heuristic: it minimises a penetration, not the time to the first collision. \ (\cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Differential drive] A wheeled robot commanded by a translational speed $v$ and a rotational speed $\omega$; with both constant it moves on a circular arc of radius $v/\omega$. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Dijkstra's algorithm] The algorithm that computes the cheapest cost from one source to every vertex of a graph with non-negative edge costs by repeatedly settling the open vertex with the smallest tentative cost. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Disagreement vector] $\vect{\delta}=\vect{x}-\bar x\vect{1}$, the distance of the states from agreement; it decays like $e^{-\lambda_2 t}$ under the consensus protocol. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Disappear-at-target] The convention in which an agent is removed from the graph the moment it first reaches its goal; not used in this book. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Discrete-time consensus] $\vect{x}_{k+1}=(\mat{I}-\eps\mat{L})\vect{x}_k$, the sampled version of the protocol; it converges for $0<\eps<2/\lambda_n$, and $\eps<1/d_{\max}$ is the sufficient bound every drone can check locally. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Displacement-based formation control] $\dot{\pos}_i=\sum_{j\in N_i}(\pos_j-\pos_i-\vect{d}_{ij})$ with desired relative positions $\vect{d}_{ij}=\vect{o}_j-\vect{o}_i$; it is consensus on the shifted variables $\pos_i-\vect{o}_i$ and converges to the formation up to a translation. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Distance-based formation control] Formation control that prescribes only inter-drone distances, needs no common frame, defines the shape up to rotation and reflection, and requires a rigid formation graph. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Dominance] $\hcost_2$ dominates $\hcost_1$ if $\hcost_2\ge\hcost_1$ everywhere; the more informed admissible heuristic expands no more nodes with $\fcost<C^*$. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Double integrator] The motion model in which the control input is the acceleration, so that the state consists of position and velocity. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Drift $d_i(t)$] The distance between a drone and its reference position; a bound $d_{\max}$ on the drift is one of the two exits from the Avoiding state into Replanning. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Dynamic window] The set $V_d$ of velocities a robot can reach from its current velocity within one control interval under its acceleration limits; DWA searches only inside it. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Early exit] Stopping a search when the target is popped from the queue, never when it is first discovered. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[ECBS] Enhanced conflict-based search: \cbs with focal search at the low level (conflict-avoiding paths within $w$ of the agent's optimum, returned with a lower bound) and at the high level (\Open by $\mathrm{LB}(N)$, \Focal by conflicts); its solutions cost at most $w\,C^*$. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Edge conflict] Two agents traversing the same edge in the same direction in the same time step; it implies a vertex conflict at the start of the step. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Edge constraint] A tuple $\langle a,u,v,t\rangle$ forbidding agent $a$ to move from $u$ to $v$ between times $t$ and $t+1$; reserving the reverse of every move of a planned path prevents swaps. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[EECBS] \ecbs with explicit estimation search at the high level, estimates learned online during the search, and the \cbs improvements (bypass, cardinal conflicts, symmetry reasoning, high-level heuristics); keeps the bound $w$ and scales to hundreds of agents. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Effect size $d_z$] The mean of the paired differences divided by their standard deviation; a unit-free measure of how large a difference is relative to its scenario-to-scenario variability. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Effective sample size] $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/\sum_i (w^{(i)})^2$, a number between $1$ and $N$ that measures how evenly the weight is spread; resampling is triggered when it falls below a threshold such as $N/2$. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Epsilon schedule] The sequence $\eps_1>\eps_2>\dots>\eps_K=1$ of inflation factors that \arastar runs through; it fixes the time to the first path, the number of published improvements and the total work. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Exact penalty] A linear slack weight $w$ larger than every Lagrange multiplier of the hard problem, for which the soft solution coincides with the hard one whenever the latter is feasible. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Execution log] The record of one run: positions of drones and intruders at every sampling instant, the state of each drone's state machine, the computation time of every decision and the events (replans), from which all metrics are computed. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Executive] The per-drone state machine that runs every control cycle and decides which layer is in charge: it follows the plan, hands the velocity to the local layer when a predicted conflict is inside the safety horizon, reconnects to the plan when the conflict has cleared, replans when reconnection fails, and re-checks conflicts after every change of a path. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Expansion] One non-stale pop from the priority queue together with the generation of the successors of the popped vertex; the unit in which the work of a search is counted. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Experiment matrix] The factors of an evaluation (drones, intruders, prediction quality, avoidance strategy, constraints) with their levels; a cell is one level of every factor, and a full factorial runs every cell while a fractional design runs a chosen subset such as one factor at a time around a base cell. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Explicit estimation search (EES)] A bounded-suboptimal search that orders nodes by a lower bound, by an inadmissible estimate of the final solution cost, and by a distance-to-go estimate, and chooses among the three fronts while keeping every expanded solution within $w$ of the lower bound. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Extended Kalman filter (EKF)] The Kalman filter applied to the tangents of $f$ at the previous estimate and of $h$ at the prediction, with the Jacobians $\mat{F}_k$ and $\mat{H}_k$ in place of the linear model matrices; exact for linear models, biased when the functions curve across the belief. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Feasibility solver] A method such as Push-and-Swap or Push-and-Rotate that returns some conflict-free plan whenever one exists (with at least two empty vertices) but gives no bound on its cost. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Feasible velocity set] The reachable velocities $\norm{\vel}\le v_{\max}$ minus the union of the truncated velocity obstacles of all obstacles; the local rule picks the feasible velocity closest to the preferred one. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Flocking] Olfati-Saber's controller with a gradient term (separation and cohesion from a smooth pairwise potential), velocity alignment (consensus on velocities) and navigation feedback towards a target; the formal descendant of Reynolds' boids. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Flocking rules] Reynolds's separation, alignment and cohesion: repel close neighbours, match their average velocity, and move towards their centroid; alignment is a velocity consensus and cohesion plus separation a pairwise spacing potential. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[FOCAL list] The band $\set{n\in\Open:\fcost(n)\le w\,\fcost_{\min}}$ of a focal search, kept as a second heap ordered by the secondary heuristic and refilled from \Open whenever $\fcost_{\min}$ rises. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Focal search ($\astar_\eps$)] Best-first search that keeps \Open ordered by an admissible $\fcost=\gcost+\hcost$ and expands, among the open nodes with $\fcost\le w\,\fcost_{\min}$, the one preferred by a secondary heuristic; its solution costs at most $w\,C^*$ whatever the secondary heuristic is. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Following conflict] One agent entering, at time $t+1$, the vertex that another agent occupied at time $t$; allowed in this book because synchronous motion keeps a one-edge gap at every integer time. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Formation and communication-range constraints] Requirements $\norm{\pos^i_k-\pos^j_k-\vect{d}_{ij}}\le e_{\max}$ and $\norm{\pos^i_k-\pos^j_k}\le R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ on pairs of drones, convex discs around a moving centre that MPC enforces through inscribed polygons. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Formation error] $e_F=\sqrt{\frac{1}{\abs{E_F}}\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_F}\norm{\pos_j-\pos_i-\vect{d}_{ij}}^2}$, the RMS violation of the desired displacements over the edges of the formation graph; translation invariant and zero exactly on the formation. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Free distance] The distance along a rollout to the first obstacle inflated by the robot radius, capped at the sensing range $d_{\max}$. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Gaussian negative log-likelihood] The loss $\sum_d[\log\sigma_d+(y_d-\mu_d)^2/(2\sigma_d^2)]$ for a read-out that predicts a mean and a standard deviation per step, minimised by the conditional mean and the conditional variance. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Global lower bound $\mathrm{LB}$] The smallest $\mathrm{LB}(N)=\sum_i\mathrm{LB}_i(N)$ over the open CT nodes; it never exceeds $C^*$, so a conflict-free node with $\cost\le w\,\mathrm{LB}$ is $w$-suboptimal, and $\cost/\mathrm{LB}$ is the bound proven by a run. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Global planner] A planner that computes a complete route from start to goal from a map of all known obstacles; in the hybrid architecture, the multi-agent planner that produces the nominal paths. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[GNRON] Goals non-reachable with obstacles nearby: when the goal lies inside the influence region of an obstacle, the repulsion at the goal is non-zero and the minimum of $U$ moves away from the goal; the standard fix multiplies the repulsive term by $\norm{\pos-\pos_{\mathrm{g}}}^n$. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Goal bias] The probability $p_{\mathrm{goal}}$ with which \textsc{Sample} returns the goal instead of a uniform configuration; small values ($0.05$--$0.1$) speed the search up, large values make the tree greedy and trapped. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Goal region] The ball of radius $r_{\mathrm{goal}}$ around the goal point; the search ends when a vertex enters it, since continuous samples never hit a point exactly. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Goal-stay test (goal-occupied-later test)] The low-level rule that a path may end at the goal at time $t$ only if no vertex constraint forbids the goal at any time $\ge t$, because the agent stays there for ever afterwards. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Goal-stay time] The last time $t_\gamma$ at which the goal is constrained; space-time \astar may finish at $(\gamma,t)$ only if $t>t_\gamma$, so that the agent can stay there for ever. \ (\cref{ch:ch04}, \cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Graph Laplacian] $\mat{L}=\mat{D}-\mat{A}$, the degree matrix minus the adjacency matrix; symmetric, positive semidefinite, with $\mat{L}\vect{1}=\vect{0}$ and $\vect{x}\T\mat{L}\vect{x}=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}(x_i-x_j)^2$. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Harmonic potential] A potential satisfying Laplace's equation $\nabla^2U=0$ in the free space; by the maximum principle it has no interior local minima, but it must be computed globally on a grid. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[HCA*] Hierarchical Cooperative \astar: Cooperative \astar with the exact static distance to the goal, computed by a backward search on the map without agents, as heuristic. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Heading term] $1-\theta/\pi$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the candidate velocity and the direction to the target seen from the predicted position; it rewards progress towards the goal or a lookahead point. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Heuristic] A function $\hcost(n)$ that estimates the cost from $n$ to the goal without searching; \astar adds it to the cost so far and expands the node with the smallest sum $\fcost=\gcost+\hcost$. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Horizon of a plan] The largest time index $T=\max_i T_i$ that any path of the plan mentions explicitly; it is at least the makespan and equals it only when no path ends with waits at its goal; no vertex or swapping conflict can first appear after it. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Hybrid architecture] The four-layer design of the book: a global swarm planner, a prediction layer, a local safety layer and a replanning layer, tied together by a five-step decision logic. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Hybrid collision-avoidance architecture] The four-layer design of the drone system: a global swarm planner (\cbs/\ecbs) for the nominal time-indexed paths, a prediction layer (Kalman filter/LSTM) for unknown objects, a local safety layer (\orca/DWA) for short avoidance manoeuvres, and a replanning layer (\dstarlite/\astar) from the current state, joined by a per-drone executive. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Hybrid world model] The shared representation of the layers: a grid with discrete time (paths with their start times, the reservation table, the blocked layers) and continuous positions, velocities and predictions, with one clock and one frame and explicit conversions between the two sides. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Hysteresis (DWA)] Keeping the current command unless the best candidate beats its score by a margin $\eta$; it damps the oscillation between two nearly equal commands but does not remove a trap. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Importance weight] The factor that corrects a sample drawn from a proposal distribution so that the weighted set represents the target distribution; in the bootstrap filter it is proportional to the accumulated measurement likelihoods. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[ImprovePath] The inner loop of \arastar: expand the state with the smallest $\fcost_\eps$ until the goal's key is no larger than every key in \Open; each state is expanded at most once per call and the result is an $\eps$-suboptimal path. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[INCONS list] The states that were expanded in the current iteration and whose $\gcost$ was lowered afterwards; \arastar records the improvement but does not re-expand them until the next iteration, when they are merged into \Open. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Inconsistent state] A state whose $\gcost$-value has been lowered since it was last expanded (or that has never been expanded); the set of inconsistent states is exactly $\Open\cup\textsc{Incons}$, and only they can still improve the search. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Incremental linear program] The randomised algorithm that finds the point of an intersection of half-planes and a disc closest to a given point by adding the half-planes one at a time and, whenever the current optimum violates the new one, solving a one-dimensional program on its boundary line; expected linear time in the number of half-planes. \ (\cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Incremental search] A search that reuses the previous search when the graph changes slightly, instead of starting over; the basis of replanning with \dstarlite. \ (\cref{ch:ch01}, \cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Incumbent] The best solution with integral values found so far during branch-and-bound; every node whose bound is not better is pruned. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Independence detection] A wrapper that plans groups of agents separately and merges two groups into one joint search only when their plans conflict; optimal whenever the group solver is optimal. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Individual policy] A rule $\phi_i$ that moves agent $i$ one step along a shortest path to its goal from any cell; following all policies from a configuration gives the policy path, whose cost equals the sum heuristic. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Inflated safety radius $d^{\mathrm{safe}}_h$] The required separation $R_{\mathrm{safe}} = r_A + r_B + \Delta r$ plus $\kappa_p\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(\mat{\Sigma}_h)}$, the radius of the disc that contains the $p$-confidence ellipse of the prediction at step $h$; keeping this distance from the predicted mean is a per-step chance constraint with probability $p$. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Inflation factor] The weight $\eps\ge1$ that \arastar puts on the heuristic in its key $\fcost_\eps=\gcost+\eps\,\hcost$; a large $\eps$ makes the search greedy and fast, $\eps=1$ makes it plain \astar. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Influence distance] The radius $\rho_0$ beyond which an obstacle exerts no repulsion; the repulsive potential and its gradient both vanish at $\rho=\rho_0$, so $U$ is continuously differentiable. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Informed RRT*] \rrtstar that, once a solution of cost $c_{\mathrm{best}}$ exists, samples the informed set uniformly by mapping the unit ball through $x=\mat{C}\mat{L}\vect{x}_{\mathrm{ball}}+\vect{x}_{\mathrm{centre}}$. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Informed set] $\set{x:\norm{x-x_{\mathrm{init}}}+\norm{x-x_{\mathrm{goal}}}\le c_{\mathrm{best}}}$, the only region in which a path cheaper than the current best can pass; the analogue of the region $\fcost\le C^*$ of \astar. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Innovation] $\vect{y}_k=\meas_k-\mat{H}\hat{\state}^-_k$, the part of the measurement the prediction did not anticipate; its covariance is $\mat{S}_k=\mat{H}\mat{P}^-_k\mat{H}\T+\mat{R}$, and a consistent filter has zero-mean, white innovations with that covariance. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Inter-agent repulsion] A pairwise repulsive term between drones with clearance $\rho_{ij}=\norm{\pos_i-\pos_j}-2r$, the potential-field form of Reynolds's separation rule. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Intruder] An unknown, non-cooperative moving object, usually another drone, that appears during the flight and whose future motion is uncertain. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Jacobian] The matrix $\partial g_i/\partial x_j$ of first derivatives of a vector function, one row per output; it is the linear map that best approximates the function near a point, with an error of second order in the displacement. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Joint configuration] A tuple $v = (v^1, \dots, v^k)$ giving the cell of every agent; the vertices of the joint graph are the collision-free configurations and its edges the joint moves without vertex or swap conflicts. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Joint state space] The set of $|V|^k$ configurations of $k$ agents on $|V|$ cells, searched by joint \astar with up to $(b+1)^k$ successors per node; its size is what makes coupled search hopeless beyond a few agents. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Joseph form] The covariance update $(\mat{I}-\Kgain\mat{H})\mat{P}^-(\mat{I}-\Kgain\mat{H})\T+\Kgain\mat{R}\Kgain\T$, valid for any gain and always symmetric positive semidefinite; it equals $(\mat{I}-\Kgain\mat{H})\mat{P}^-$ for the Kalman gain. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[$k$-nearest RRT*] The variant of \rrtstar whose \textsc{Near} set is the $k_n=\lceil k_{\mathrm{RRG}}\log n\rceil$ nearest vertices with $k_{\mathrm{RRG}}>e(1+1/d)$; it needs no estimate of $\mu(\Xfree)$. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Kalman extrapolation] Running the predict step of the constant-velocity Kalman filter $h$ times without updates; the optimal linear predictor under its noise model, with a covariance that grows with the horizon. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Kalman filter] The recursive estimator for a linear-Gaussian state-space model: it keeps a Gaussian belief $\Normal(\hat{\state}_k,\mat{P}_k)$ and alternates a predict step through the motion model and an update step with the measurement; it is the exact posterior and the minimum-mean-square-error estimator, and the best linear estimator when the noise is not Gaussian. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Kalman gain] $\Kgain_k=\mat{P}^-_k\mat{H}\T\mat{S}_k\inv$, the matrix by which the innovation corrects the predicted mean; it weights prediction and measurement by their precisions and corrects unmeasured state components through their covariance with the measured ones. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[kd-tree] A binary tree that splits points along coordinate axes and answers nearest-neighbour queries in $\bigO{\log n}$ expected time in low dimension, against $\bigO{n}$ for a linear scan. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Key modifier] The running sum $k_m$ of the heuristic distances the robot has moved between repairs; added to every new key of \dstarlite, it turns the keys already in the queue into lower bounds instead of forcing the heap to be rebuilt. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Kinodynamic RRT] RRT over states $(\pos,\vel)$ in which \textsc{Steer} is replaced by forward simulation of sampled controls and \textsc{Nearest} uses a weighted state-space metric; the result is a trajectory that obeys the dynamics. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[KKT conditions] Stationarity of the Lagrangian, primal and dual feasibility and complementary slackness; necessary for a local minimiser under a constraint qualification and sufficient for convex problems, with the multipliers measuring the cost of tightening each active constraint. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Lazy deletion] The priority-queue idiom of pushing a duplicate entry instead of decreasing a key, and skipping entries that are stale when they are popped. \ (\cref{ch:ch02}, \cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Leader-follower (pinned) consensus] Consensus in which some drones add a term $b_i(\vect{r}-\vect{x}_i)$ pulling them to an external reference $\vect{r}$; with a connected graph and at least one pinned drone all states converge to $\vect{r}$. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Lifelong Planning A* (LPA*)] The incremental version of \astar for a fixed start and goal: it keeps $\gcost$- and $\rhs$-values across edge-cost changes and re-expands only locally inconsistent vertices. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Limited neighbours] The successors of a node in \mstar: the agents in the collision set take any move, all other agents take their policy step, so a node has $(b+1)^{|C(v)|}$ successors. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Linear program (LP)] Minimisation of a linear objective subject to linear equalities, inequalities and bounds; its feasible set is a polyhedron and its optimum is attained at a vertex. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Linear-Gaussian state-space model] $\state_k=\mat{F}\state_{k-1}+\mat{B}\ctrl_k+\vect{w}_k$, $\meas_k=\mat{H}\state_k+\vect{v}_k$ with independent Gaussian noises $\vect{w}_k\sim\Normal(\vect{0},\mat{Q})$ and $\vect{v}_k\sim\Normal(\vect{0},\mat{R})$; $\mat{F}$ is the state-transition matrix and $\mat{H}$ the measurement matrix. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Linearisation error] The difference between the Gaussian produced by the tangent of a nonlinear function and the true (non-Gaussian, ``banana'') distribution of its output; it grows with the curvature of the function times the width of the belief. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Linearised avoidance constraint] The half-plane $\vect{n}_k\T(\pos_k-\hat{\vect{o}}_k)\ge r_k$ that replaces the non-convex disc constraint $\norm{\pos_k-\hat{\vect{o}}_k}\ge r_k$ at step $k$, with the normal $\vect{n}_k$ taken from the previous plan; it is convex and conservative. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Local consistency] The property $\gcost(s)=\rhs(s)$; only locally inconsistent vertices are in the priority queue and need work. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Local minimum (DWA)] A state from which the greedy, memoryless rule keeps the robot at rest or shuttling although a collision-free path to the goal exists; the reason why DWA is not complete. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Local minimum (of a potential field)] A point other than the goal where the attractive and repulsive forces cancel and the potential rises in every direction; a gradient-descent robot that enters its basin stops there. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Local planner] A planner that looks only a few seconds ahead, uses only what the sensors see, and outputs the next velocity or manoeuvre. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Longest path first] The ordering rule that plans agents in decreasing length of their independent shortest paths; rarely fails but produces expensive plans. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Lookahead point] The point at a fixed arc length ahead of the robot's projection on a global path, used as the target of the heading term to keep a local planner out of local minima. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[LP relaxation] The linear program obtained from a mixed-integer program by dropping the integrality constraints; its optimal value bounds the integer optimum, which branch and bound exploits by splitting on a fractional variable and pruning subproblems whose bound cannot beat the incumbent. \ (\cref{ch:appB}, \cref{ch:ch22})
\item[LSTM cell] A recurrent unit whose cell state is updated by gated addition, $\vect{c}_t=\vect{f}_t\odot\vect{c}_{t-1}+\vect{i}_t\odot\tilde{\vect{c}}_t$, with forget, input and output gates in $(0,1)$ produced by logistic functions; the direct gradient path through $\vect{c}$ is $\diag(\vect{f}_t)$. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Mahalanobis distance] $d(\state)=\sqrt{(\state-\vect{\mu})\T\mat{\Sigma}\inv(\state-\vect{\mu})}$, the distance from the mean measured in units of the covariance; for a Gaussian vector $d^2$ is $\chi^2_n$ distributed, which is the basis of gating. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Makespan] The number of time steps until the last agent of a plan has reached its goal for good. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Meta-agent CBS (MA-CBS)] A variant that merges agents which conflict more than $B$ times into a meta-agent planned jointly at the low level, interpolating between plain \cbs ($B = \infty$) and Standley's independence detection ($B = 0$), in which every pair is merged at its first conflict, so each group of interacting agents is solved by a joint-space \astar while agents that never conflict are still planned alone. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Minimum separation $d_{\min}$] The smallest distance between any two agents over a run, evaluated with linear motion between samples; reported as a median with IQR and a 5th percentile, and turned into the near-miss rate by comparing it with the safety radius. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Minimum-fuel objective] The total velocity change $\dt \sum_k \norm{\ctrl_k}_1$ of a trajectory, linearised with one auxiliary variable per input component. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Minkowski sum] The set of all sums $\vect{a}+\vect{b}$ with $\vect{a}$ in one set and $\vect{b}$ in another; inflating an obstacle by the robot's radius is a Minkowski sum with a disc. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[MIP gap] The relative difference between the incumbent's cost and the best remaining bound; zero certifies optimality, and a time-limited solve reports the gap it reached. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Mixed-integer linear program (MILP)] An LP in which some variables are restricted to integers; with binary variables it encodes choices, either-or conditions, switches and assignments. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Model predictive control (MPC)] A feedback controller that, at every step, solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem from the measured state, applies the first input and repeats; constraints are part of the optimisation rather than an afterthought. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Multi-source Dijkstra] Dijkstra's algorithm started with several sources at cost zero, which yields the cost to the nearest source for every vertex. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Multi-valued decision diagram (MDD)] For an agent and a cost $c$, the layered graph whose level $t$ contains every cell that lies on some path of cost $c$ at time $t$; a conflict is cardinal when both agents have a single cell at its level. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Multimodal prediction] A prediction that puts probability mass on several distinct futures (mixture density outputs, sampled rollouts of a GAN or CVAE, ensembles), needed because a squared-error predictor converges to the conditional mean, which averages the modes. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Naive plan] The plan made of independent shortest paths, one per agent, ignoring all other agents; its costs are lower bounds for every valid solution. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Narrow-passage problem] The growth of the expected number of iterations like $(1/w)^{d}$ for a passage of width $w$, because uniform samples rarely fall into it. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Navigation function] A potential on a bounded free space with a unique minimum at the goal, whose other critical points are non-degenerate saddles; Rimon and Koditschek construct one explicitly for sphere worlds. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Near] The set $\Near(V,x,r)=\set{v\in V:\norm{v-x}\le r}$ of tree vertices within the connection radius of a point; the candidate set of \textsc{ChooseParent} and \textsc{Rewire} in \rrtstar. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Non-cooperative agent] An agent that does not share the avoidance rules of the swarm; a drone that meets it must take the full responsibility for avoiding it. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Non-cooperative obstacle] An object that does not react to the agent, such as an unknown drone or a bird; it is avoided with the plain velocity obstacle (full responsibility), not with a reciprocal one. \ (\cref{ch:ch12}, \cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Normal equations] The linear system $\mat{A}\T\mat{A}\vect{x}=\mat{A}\T\vect{b}$ whose solution minimises $\norm{\mat{A}\vect{x}-\vect{b}}^2$; unique when $\mat{A}$ has full column rank. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Normalised innovation squared (NIS)] $d^2_k=\vect{y}_k\T\mat{S}_k\inv\vect{y}_k$, the squared Mahalanobis distance of a measurement from its prediction; chi-square with $m$ degrees of freedom for a consistent filter, used to tune $\mat{Q}$ and to gate outliers. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Observability] The property that the observability matrix $(\mat{H};\mat{H}\mat{F};\dots;\mat{H}\mat{F}^{n-1})$ has full rank, so that the state can be recovered from a finite number of noise-free measurements; without it the covariance of the unobserved components grows without bound. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Octile distance] $\max(d_x,d_y)+(\sqrt2-1)\min(d_x,d_y)$, the exact cost between two cells of an obstacle-free 8-connected grid with moves of cost $1$ and $\sqrt2$; consistent, and the standard heuristic for such grids. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Operator decomposition] Standley's device of letting the agents choose their moves one at a time through intermediate states, which cuts the branching factor of joint \astar from $(b+1)^k$ to $b+1$. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Oracle baseline] An offline optimum computed with full knowledge of the future (a MILP that sees the intruder's whole trajectory) on tiny instances; it bounds what any online strategy can achieve. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[ORCA half-plane] $\ORCA^{\ttc}_{A|B}=\set{\vel : (\vel-(\vel_A+\tfrac12\vect{u}))\cdot\vect{n}\ge0}$, the velocities permitted to $A$ with respect to $B$ for the horizon $\ttc$, where $\vect{u}$ is the smallest change of the relative velocity that reaches the boundary of $\VO^{\ttc}_{A|B}$ and $\vect{n}$ the outward normal there; in three dimensions a half-space. \ (\cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Oscillation (velocity obstacles)] The step-by-step reversal of avoidance manoeuvres that occurs when two agents apply the velocity-obstacle rule simultaneously, each assuming that the other keeps its velocity; the motivation for reciprocal velocity obstacles. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Overconsistent vertex] A vertex with $\gcost(s)>\rhs(s)$: a cheaper value is available and expanding it sets $\gcost(s)\gets\rhs(s)$, as an \astar expansion would. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Paired design] An evaluation in which every strategy runs on the same seeded scenarios and comparisons are made on the per-scenario differences, which removes the scenario-to-scenario spread from the comparison. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Pareto plot] A plot with one point per strategy and cell in the plane of an efficiency loss against a safety loss; the points not dominated by any other form the front and state the trade-off. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Parked goal] A goal cell on which an agent has arrived at time $T$ and stays for ever under stay-at-target; reserved for all $t \ge T$. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Partial replanning (local \cbs)] The repair of a conflict found by the re-check by running \cbs on the two agents in conflict only, from the next grid time, with the paths of all other drones reserved. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Particle filter] A filter that represents the belief by $N$ weighted samples, propagates them through the motion model with sampled noise, weights them by the measurement likelihood and resamples when the weights degenerate; it can represent multimodal and non-Gaussian beliefs at a cost linear in $N$. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Path-length ratio $\rho_L$] The flown path length divided by the length of the nominal plan, averaged over the drones of a run; the efficiency cost of avoidance, independent of the arena size. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Per-agent lower bound $\mathrm{LB}_i(N)$] A number stored in a CT node that is at most the cost of the cheapest path of agent $a_i$ under the node's constraints; the focal low level returns it as the $\fcost_{\min}$ of its \Open when the goal is popped. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Plan (MAPF)] A tuple of one time-indexed path per agent; viewed as a table with agents as rows and time steps as columns. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Planned conflict] A collision between two controlled drones that follows from their planned time-indexed routes alone; detected and resolved before the flight. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Polyhedron] The intersection of finitely many half-spaces; convex, with flat faces and vertices, the feasible set of every LP. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Positional encoding] Sinusoids of geometrically spaced frequencies added to the token embeddings so that attention, which is otherwise a set operation, can tell the order of the time steps. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Positive semidefinite matrix] A symmetric matrix $\mat{A}$ with $\vect{x}\T\mat{A}\vect{x}\ge0$ for all $\vect{x}$, equivalently with no negative eigenvalue, written $\mat{A}\succeq\mat{0}$; every covariance matrix is one, and $\mat{A}\succ\mat{0}$ (positive definite) additionally excludes zero eigenvalues. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Predict step] $\hat{\state}^-_k=\mat{F}\hat{\state}_{k-1}+\mat{B}\ctrl_k$, $\mat{P}^-_k=\mat{F}\mat{P}_{k-1}\mat{F}\T+\mat{Q}$: the belief pushed through the motion model, with the covariance inflated by the process noise. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Predicted time to collision $t_c$] The first look-ahead at which the margin $\norm{\tilde{\pos}_i(s) - \hat{\pos}_{T+h}} - \kappa_p\sigma(h) - R_{\mathrm{safe}}$ is negative; the trigger fires when $t_c \le \tau_h$. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Prediction] Extrapolating the estimated state of a moving object into the future, over a horizon, together with the growing uncertainty. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Prediction covariance] $\mat{P}_{k+j\mid k}=\mat{F}^j\mat{P}_k(\mat{F}^j)\T+\sum_{i<j}\mat{F}^i\mat{Q}(\mat{F}^i)\T$, the uncertainty of the state $j$ steps ahead given the measurements up to $k$; it grows without bound in $j$ and is what the safety layer inflates an intruder's radius with. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Prediction matrices] $\mat{S}_x$ and $\mat{S}_u$, built from powers of $\mat{A}$ and $\mat{B}$, that map the current state and the stacked inputs to the stacked predicted states. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Preferred velocity] $\vel^{\mathrm{pref}}$, the velocity an agent would fly if nothing were in the way, typically towards the goal or along the nominal route at the nominal speed. \ (\cref{ch:ch12}, \cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Prioritized planning] Planning the agents of a MAPF instance one after another in a priority order, each with a single-agent space-time search that treats the paths of the earlier agents as moving obstacles; fast, sound, but incomplete and suboptimal in general. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Priority order] A permutation $\sigma$ of the agents; $\sigma(1)$ is planned first and never yields to anyone, $\sigma(k)$ yields to everyone. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Priority-based search] A two-level search over partial priority orders (Ma et al.): the high level branches on a conflicting pair of agents by adding $i \prec j$ or $j \prec i$ and searches depth-first, the low level replans the affected agents in topological order against the paths of their higher-priority agents. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Probabilistic completeness] The guarantee that, when a solution with positive clearance exists, the probability of having found one after $n$ iterations tends to one as $n\to\infty$; it says nothing when no solution exists. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Probabilistic roadmap (PRM)] The multi-query counterpart of RRT: sample free configurations, connect each to its nearest neighbours by checked segments, and answer queries by graph search on the roadmap. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Prolate hyperspheroid] The shape of the informed set: an ellipse (2D) or ellipsoid of revolution (3D) with foci at the start and the goal, transverse diameter $c_{\mathrm{best}}$ and conjugate diameter $\sqrt{c_{\mathrm{best}}^2-c_{\min}^2}$. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Push (primitive)] Moving an agent along its shortest path and shifting the chain of unlocked agents in its way one step towards the nearest empty vertex off the path. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Quadratic program (QP)] Minimisation of a convex quadratic function $\tfrac12\vect{z}\T\mat{H}\vect{z}+\vect{f}\T\vect{z}$ subject to linear inequality constraints; the problem MPC with a linear model, quadratic cost and linearised constraints solves at every step. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Random restarts] Running prioritized planning with several random orders and keeping the cheapest plan that succeeds. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Range--bearing measurement] The pair $(r, \varphi)$ of distance and direction from a sensor to the intruder, $r = \norm{(x, y) - \vect{s}}$ and $\varphi = \operatorname{atan2}(y - s_y, x - s_x)$; a bearing error of $\sigma_\varphi$ radians displaces the position by about $r\sigma_\varphi$ across the line of sight. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Rapidly-exploring random tree (RRT)] A tree rooted at the start configuration that grows one vertex per random sample by moving at most $\eta$ from the nearest vertex towards the sample when that segment is collision-free; the first vertex in the goal region yields a path. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Re-opening] Moving a closed node back to \Open when a cheaper path to it is found; necessary for optimality with an admissible but inconsistent heuristic, never triggered with a consistent one. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Reactive method] A method that maps the current situation directly to an action, with little or no search. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Receding horizon] The moving window of $N$ future steps over which MPC optimises; after each step the window is shifted by one step and the plan is recomputed. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Reciprocal dance] The oscillation of two agents that avoid each other with plain velocity obstacles (both swerve, both return, both swerve) or, for RVO, that disagree about the side on which to pass; \orca removes it by fixing the share of the responsibility. \ (\cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Reciprocal velocity obstacle (RVO)] The set $\RVO_{A|B}(\vel_B,\vel_A)$ of velocities $\vel$ for which $2\vel-\vel_A$ lies in the velocity obstacle $\vel_B+\VO_{A|B}$: the velocities that $A$ must avoid when it takes half of the avoidance and trusts $B$ to take the other half; it is the velocity obstacle cone with its apex moved to $\tfrac12(\vel_A+\vel_B)$. \ (\cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Reconnection] The return to the nominal path after an avoidance manoeuvre: a straight flight to a waypoint $\pi_i[k]$ ahead on the plan, arriving at grid time $t_0^i + k + \Delta$ with a delay $\Delta \le \Delta_{\max}$, admissible when it is slow enough and clear of obstacles, of the inflated prediction and of the teammates' intended positions. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Rectangle symmetry] Two agents crossing an open rectangle in perpendicular directions whose shortest paths all pairwise conflict; the plain constraint tree grows exponentially, and barrier constraints resolve the whole rectangle in one split. \ (\cref{ch:ch09})
\item[Recursive feasibility] The property that feasibility of the MPC problem at one step implies feasibility at the next; with a terminal set and a static world it follows from the shifted plan. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Reference position $\pos^{\mathrm{ref}}_i(t)$] The continuous position that a time-indexed path prescribes at clock time $t$, obtained by linear interpolation between the centres of consecutive cells; the preferred velocity of the local layer is a pursuit of the reference a short lookahead ahead. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Relative position] $\pos_{\mathrm{rel}}=\pos_B-\pos_A$, the position of agent $B$ seen from agent $A$; with the relative velocity it determines whether two agents on constant velocities collide. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Relative velocity] $\vel_{\mathrm{rel}}=\vel_A-\vel_B$, the velocity of $A$ in the frame of $B$; two discs collide at time $t$ if and only if $\norm{\pos_{\mathrm{rel}}-t\vel_{\mathrm{rel}}}\le r_A+r_B$. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Relaxation] The update of a neighbour's tentative cost and parent pointer when a cheaper path to it through the vertex being expanded is found. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Replanning layer] The layer of the hybrid drone architecture that, when the local avoidance manoeuvre cannot rejoin the nominal route, recomputes a route from the drone's current cell with the predicted intruder region encoded as changed edge costs. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Repulsive potential] Khatib's obstacle term $U_{\mathrm{rep}}=\tfrac12 k_{\mathrm{rep}}(1/\rho-1/\rho_0)^2$ for $\rho\le\rho_0$ and $0$ otherwise, where $\rho$ is the clearance to the obstacle; its force $k_{\mathrm{rep}}(1/\rho-1/\rho_0)\rho^{-2}\nabla\rho$ grows without bound as $\rho\to0$. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Reservation table] The set of vertex and edge constraints derived from the paths of already planned agents, together with their parked goal cells, which are blocked for all later times. \ (\cref{ch:ch04}, \cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Responsibility share] The fraction $\alpha$ of the change $\vect{u}$ that an agent takes: $\tfrac12$ between agents that both run \orca, $1$ (full responsibility) against an obstacle or a non-cooperative intruder; the pairwise guarantee holds exactly when the two shares of a pair sum to one. \ (\cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Restarted weighted A*] The naive anytime search that runs weighted \astar from scratch once per inflation factor; it repeats the work of every previous run, which \arastar avoids by keeping $\gcost$-values, \Open and \textsc{Incons}. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Revised rule] The variant of prioritized planning in which each agent also treats the start cells of all lower-priority agents as static obstacles; needed for the completeness guarantee on well-formed instances. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Rewire] The \rrtstar step that makes the new vertex the parent of every near vertex whose cost-to-come it lowers through a collision-free segment, propagating the saving to all descendants of that vertex. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[rhs-value] The one-step lookahead $\rhs(s)$ of a vertex, the best value its neighbours currently imply ($\min$ over predecessors of $\gcost + $ edge cost in \lpastar, over successors in \dstarlite); it is always kept up to date. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Robustly optimal solution] An optimal path that is the limit in cost of collision-free paths with positive clearance; the assumption under which sampling-based planners can converge to it. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Rollout] The trajectory a candidate command would produce if held constant: a circular arc of radius $v/\omega$ for a differential drive, a straight segment for a drone; its free distance is the clearance of the candidate. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Rotate (primitive)] Advancing every agent on a fully occupied cycle by one position: one agent steps out into a cleared neighbouring vertex, the others advance, and it steps back in. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[RRT-Connect] A bidirectional RRT with one tree from the start and one from the goal, in which the other tree greedily repeats \textsc{Extend} towards every new vertex (\textsc{Connect}) and the trees swap roles every iteration. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Rule of three] With no event in $N$ runs the one-sided $95\,\%$ upper bound on the event probability is about $3/N$. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Safety horizon] The look-ahead time within which a predicted collision counts as a near-term risk that triggers local avoidance. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Safety horizon $\tau_h$] The look-ahead window of the trigger: a predicted conflict is inside the horizon when the predicted separation minus the uncertainty inflation drops below the safety radius within $\tau_h$ seconds; chosen at least as long as the \orca horizon and the time the drone needs to execute a velocity change. \ (\cref{ch:ch24})
\item[Sample impoverishment] The loss of diversity after resampling, when the surviving particles are copies of a few ancestors that the process noise has not yet separated; aggravated by resampling at every step and by small process noise. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Sampling-based planning] Planning in a continuous space by drawing random configurations, keeping the collision-free ones and connecting them by short collision-free segments, so that memory grows with the number of samples rather than with the size or dimension of the space. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Sanity baseline] A strategy that must fail or succeed in a known way (no avoidance collides with aimed intruders and never without them); its purpose is to validate the scenario generator and the plan, not to be beaten. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Scenario file] A \code{.scen} text file of the MAPF benchmark listing start--goal pairs as $x$ (column) and $y$ (row) coordinates on a named \code{.map} grid. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Schur complement] For a block matrix $\begin{bsmallmatrix}\mat{A}&\mat{B}\\\mat{C}&\mat{D}\end{bsmallmatrix}$ with invertible $\mat{D}$, the matrix $\mat{A}-\mat{B}\mat{D}\inv\mat{C}$; it is the top-left block of the inverse's inverse, gives the block determinant, and is the covariance of a conditional Gaussian. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\item[Second-order consensus] Consensus for double integrators, $\ddot{\pos}_i=\sum_j a_{ij}[k_p(\pos_j-\pos_i-\vect{d}_{ij})+k_v(\vel_j-\vel_i)]-k_d\vel_i$; the velocity terms provide the damping without which the swarm oscillates for ever. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Secondary heuristic $\hcost_{\Focal}$] The function that chooses the node inside the focal band; it need not be admissible or even estimate cost. In \ecbs it is the number of conflicts. \ (\cref{ch:ch10})
\item[Sequence-to-sequence predictor] An encoder LSTM that summarises the observed displacements and a decoder LSTM that rolls the future out one step at a time from the handed-over state, with a read-out per step. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Settled vertex] A vertex that has been popped from the priority queue and added to the closed set; its tentative cost is then final. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Shortcutting] Path post-processing that replaces the part of a path between two points by the straight segment when that segment is collision-free; it never increases the length but cannot carry the path across an obstacle. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Shortest-path distance] The smallest cost $\delta(u,v)$ of any path from $u$ to $v$, taken to be infinite when no path exists. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Shortest-path tree] The tree formed by the parent pointers of a single-source search; following them from any vertex back to the source traces a shortest path. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Sigma points] The $2n+1$ points $\bar{\state}$ and $\bar{\state} \pm \vect{l}_i$, where $\vect{l}_i$ are the columns of a square root of $(n+\lambda)\mat{P}$ with $\lambda = \alpha^2(n+\kappa) - n$; their weighted mean and covariance equal $\bar{\state}$ and $\mat{P}$ exactly. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Social pooling] The Social-LSTM construction that sums the hidden states of the neighbours in each cell of a grid centred on the agent and feeds the embedded grid to the agent's LSTM. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Soft constraint] A constraint $g(\vect{z})\le s$ with a slack variable $s\ge0$ that is penalised in the cost; it keeps the problem feasible and gives the least violation when the hard version cannot be satisfied. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Space-time A*] \astar over states $(v,t)$ with a wait action, vertex and edge constraints, a goal-stay test and a time horizon; the low-level search of prioritized planning and of conflict-based search. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Space-time state] A pair $(v,t)$ of a vertex and a discrete time index; the states of the time-expanded graph. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Stale entry] A priority-queue entry of a vertex that has already been settled with a smaller key; lazy deletion discards it when it is popped. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Stay-at-target] The convention in which an agent that has reached its goal remains there forever and keeps blocking the vertex; the cost of its path is the time of its last arrival. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Step size] The largest length $\eta$ of a new edge: \textsc{Steer} moves from the nearest vertex towards the sample by at most $\eta$. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Stiffness] The largest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\max}$ of the Hessian of $U$ at a point; the explicit update $\pos\gets\pos+\dt\,\vect{F}$ is stable near a minimum only if $\dt\,\lambda_{\max}<2$, and stiffness grows steeply in narrow passages. \ (\cref{ch:ch15})
\item[Strong $\delta$-clearance] A path all of whose points are at distance at least $\delta$ from the obstacles. \ (\cref{ch:ch17})
\item[Subdimensional expansion] Wagner and Choset's principle of searching the joint space along the individual policies and raising the dimension of the search only where a collision has been found. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Suboptimality certificate] The bound $\eps'=\min\bigl(\eps,\ \gcost(\gamma)/\min_{n\in\Open\cup\textsc{Incons}}(\gcost(n)+\hcost(n))\bigr)$ published with every \arastar path; the path costs at most $\eps'\,C^*$, and usually $\eps'$ is much smaller than $\eps$. \ (\cref{ch:ch06})
\item[Success rate (with a cap)] The fraction of runs that finish within a time or computation cap without collision; finished-run metrics are averaged over successful runs only and reported next to it, or replaced by a penalised score such as PAR-2. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Sum of costs] The total number of time steps, summed over all agents, until each agent has reached its goal for good. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Swap (primitive)] Exchanging two adjacent agents at a vertex of degree at least three with two empty neighbours: a multipush to the vertex, six exchange moves, and the reversal of the preparation with the agents exchanged; $4d + 6$ moves when the junction is $d$ steps away. \ (\cref{ch:ch11})
\item[Swapping conflict] Two agents traversing the same edge in opposite directions in the same time step, exchanging vertices; forbidden in this book. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Switching topology] A communication graph that changes with time (drones move, packets are lost); consensus still converges if the union of the graphs over bounded time windows is connected. \ (\cref{ch:ch23})
\item[Symmetry breaking] An extra constraint that removes mirror-image solutions of equal cost from a MILP, such as fixing on which side one drone passes another, so that branch-and-bound explores half the tree. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Systematic resampling] Resampling with one uniform draw $u \in [0, 1/N)$ and the grid $u + (j-1)/N$ over the cumulative weights, which copies each particle $\lfloor Nw^{(i)}\rfloor$ or $\lceil Nw^{(i)}\rceil$ times in $\bigO{N}$ time. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Tangent half-angle] $\theta=\arcsin(R/d)$ with $R=r_A+r_B$ and $d=\norm{\pos_{\mathrm{rel}}}$, the angle between the axis of the collision cone and each of its boundary rays. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Teacher forcing] Feeding the decoder the true previous displacement during training instead of its own prediction; fast to train but subject to exposure bias, the mismatch between training inputs and free-running inputs. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Tentative cost] The cost $\gcost(v)$ of the best path to $v$ found so far; it never underestimates the true distance and only ever decreases. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Terminal cost] The weight $\state_N\T\mat{P}\state_N$ on the last predicted state, usually the LQR cost-to-go from the Riccati equation, which stands in for the cost beyond the horizon and underlies the stability proof of MPC. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Tie-breaking] The rule that orders nodes with equal $\fcost$; preferring the larger $\gcost$ (key $(\fcost,-\gcost,\mathit{counter})$) makes \astar dive along one optimal path instead of sweeping the whole $\fcost=C^*$ band. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Time horizon] The largest time $T_{\max}$ for which space-time states are generated; $T_{\max}=H+1+D$, with $H$ the last constrained time and $D$ the largest static distance to the goal, keeps the search complete and finite. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Time horizon (ORCA)] $\ttc$, the time span for which the chosen velocities are guaranteed collision-free; recomputed every $\dt\ll\ttc$, with a shorter horizon $\ttc_{\mathrm{obst}}$ for static obstacles. \ (\cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Time horizon (velocity obstacle)] The time $\ttc$ beyond which predicted collisions are ignored by the local avoidance rule; it must exceed the decision interval and allow the next manoeuvre. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Time of closest approach] The time at which two objects moving with constant velocities are closest to each other. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Time to collision] $t_c(\vel_{\mathrm{rel}})$, the first time at which the discs touch, the smaller root of $(\vel\cdot\vel)t^2-2(\pos\cdot\vel)t+(\pos\cdot\pos-R^2)=0$; infinite if the discriminant is negative or $\pos\cdot\vel\le0$. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Time-expanded flow formulation] The integer program of Yu and LaValle for MAPF: one unit of flow per agent on the time-expanded graph, with capacity-one states and anti-swap rows. \ (\cref{ch:ch22})
\item[Time-expanded graph] The graph whose vertices are the space-time states and whose edges are the move and wait actions between consecutive time layers. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Time-indexed occupancy region] The sequence of $p$-probability ellipses $\mathcal{E}_h(p)$ of a predicted distribution, one per horizon step, from which the planners derive an inflated radius, a cost region or a chance-constraint margin. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[Time-indexed path] A sequence of vertices $\pi_i[0],\dots,\pi_i[T_i]$ from start to goal in which consecutive entries are equal (a wait) or adjacent in the graph (a move). \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Tracking] Estimating the current state of a moving object, typically position and velocity, from a sequence of noisy measurements. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Trajectory] A time-parametrised curve in continuous time, represented in the book by waypoints with velocities. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Trajectory prediction] Mapping the last $T_{\mathrm{obs}}$ observed positions of an agent (and possibly its neighbours) to its next $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ positions, ideally as a distribution per horizon step. \ (\cref{ch:ch20})
\item[True-distance heuristic] The exact cost-to-go $\hcost^*(v)=\delta(v,t)$ computed by backward Dijkstra; it is consistent, exact on the static map and still admissible in space-time and under constraints. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Truncated velocity obstacle] $\VO^{\ttc}_{A|B}$, the velocities that collide within the horizon $\ttc$; the wedge with its tip cut off by the disc of centre $\vel_B+\pos_{\mathrm{rel}}/\ttc$ and radius $R/\ttc$. \ (\cref{ch:ch12}, \cref{ch:ch13})
\item[Two-component key] The priority $[\min(\gcost,\rhs)+\hcost;\ \min(\gcost,\rhs)]$ of a queued vertex, compared lexicographically; the first component is the $\fcost$-value of \astar, the second breaks ties toward smaller values so that stale values are retracted before their dependents are expanded. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Two-point initialisation] Starting a track from two measurements one step apart with $\hat{\state}_0=(\meas_b,(\meas_b-\meas_a)/\dt)$ and the matching covariance $\begin{psmallmatrix}\mat{R}&\mat{R}/\dt\\ \mat{R}/\dt&2\mat{R}/\dt^2\end{psmallmatrix}$. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Underconsistent vertex] A vertex with $\gcost(s)<\rhs(s)$: its stored value relies on a cost that no longer exists; expanding it retracts the value ($\gcost(s)\gets\infty$) before it can propagate further. \ (\cref{ch:ch05})
\item[Unexpected obstacle] An object that was not part of the plan and is observed only during the flight; it must be handled in real time from a prediction of its motion. \ (\cref{ch:ch01})
\item[Uniform-cost search] Dijkstra's algorithm with an early exit: the search stops as soon as the target is popped, and only vertices no farther than the target are settled. \ (\cref{ch:ch03})
\item[Unscented Kalman filter (UKF)] The filter that replaces both linearisations of the EKF by unscented transforms and uses the cross-covariance between state and predicted measurement in place of $\mat{P}\mat{H}\T$; it needs no Jacobians. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Unscented transform] The approximation of the mean, covariance and cross-covariance of $g(\state)$ obtained by mapping $2n+1$ sigma points through $g$ and combining the images with the weights $W^{(m)}$ and $W^{(c)}$; exact for affine $g$ and second-order accurate in the mean for any smooth $g$. \ (\cref{ch:ch19})
\item[Valid solution] A plan whose paths are legal and which has no vertex or swapping conflict at any time under stay-at-target. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Validation gate] The ellipsoid $d^2\le\gamma$ around the predicted measurement, with $\gamma$ a chi-square quantile; measurements outside it are treated as missing, and with several tracks the gates decide which measurement may be assigned to which track. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Velocity obstacle] $\VO_{A|B}(\vel_B)=\vel_B\oplus CC_{A|B}$, the set of velocities of $A$ that lead to a collision with $B$ if $B$ keeps its velocity; the collision cone with its apex moved to $\vel_B$. \ (\cref{ch:ch12})
\item[Velocity space] The space of velocity commands, $(v,\omega)$ for a differential drive and $(v_x,v_y,v_z)$ for a velocity-controlled drone, in which DWA searches. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Velocity term] The candidate speed divided by $v_{\max}$; it rewards fast motion. \ (\cref{ch:ch14})
\item[Vertex conflict] Two agents occupying the same vertex at the same time step; forbidden in this book. \ (\cref{ch:ch07})
\item[Vertex constraint] A tuple $\langle a,v,t\rangle$ forbidding agent $a$ to occupy cell $v$ at time $t$. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Voronoi bias] The property that a vertex of the tree is chosen for extension with probability equal to the relative volume of its Voronoi region, so that vertices facing large unexplored regions are extended most often. \ (\cref{ch:ch16})
\item[Wait action] The action that keeps an agent at its current vertex for one time step. \ (\cref{ch:ch02})
\item[Wait-then-go path] The witness path of the completeness proof: wait at the start until all higher-priority agents are parked, then follow the endpoint-free path. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[Warm start] Initialising the QP solver with the previous plan shifted by one step, which typically halves the number of iterations. \ (\cref{ch:ch21})
\item[Weighted A*] \astar with the key $\gcost+w\hcost$ for $w\ge1$; it expands fewer nodes and returns a path of cost at most $w\,C^*$. \ (\cref{ch:ch04})
\item[Well-formed instance] An instance in which every agent has a path from its start to its goal that visits no start or goal of another agent; the revised algorithm succeeds on it for every order. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[WHCA*] Windowed Hierarchical Cooperative \astar: the reservation table is respected only for the next $w$ steps, a prefix of each plan is executed, and all agents replan with rotated priorities; used for lifelong and online planning, without guarantees. \ (\cref{ch:ch08})
\item[White-noise acceleration] The process-noise model in which the acceleration is continuous-time white noise of intensity $q$ (m$^2$/s$^3$), giving per axis $\mat{Q}=q\begin{psmallmatrix}\dt^3/3&\dt^2/2\\ \dt^2/2&\dt\end{psmallmatrix}$; $q$ is a rate, independent of the sampling interval. \ (\cref{ch:ch18})
\item[Wilson interval] A confidence interval for a proportion $x/N$ that stays informative at $0/N$ and $N/N$; for $0/20$ it is $[0, 0.16]$. \ (\cref{ch:ch25})
\item[Woodbury identity] The matrix inversion lemma $(\mat{A}+\mat{U}\mat{C}\mat{V})\inv=\mat{A}\inv-\mat{A}\inv\mat{U}(\mat{C}\inv+\mat{V}\mat{A}\inv\mat{U})\inv\mat{V}\mat{A}\inv$, which trades a large inverse for a small one and links the covariance and information forms of the Kalman update. \ (\cref{ch:appB})
\end{description}
